title: kei.policy-bundle/v1
description: The policy bundle a runtime installation's PEP (kei-connector-runtime) enforces (ADR-026). The root schema is the canonical JSON object served by the catalog and validated/persisted by the runtime. Transport integrity is provided by the exact-byte SHA-256 digest and authenticated HTTPS. The $id is an identifier, not a fetchable URL. ADR-029 adds the optional harness command fields (harnesses, harness_match_semantics), which kei harness sync renders into native harness permissions.

bundle_version.description: Issuance sequence for this installation. Strictly increasing, never reused; every issuance (including a re-sign with unchanged policy) takes the next value. A runtime never activates a bundle_version lower than or equal to the highest it has activated.

policy_revision.description: The workspace's policy revision this bundle was built from. Increases on every policy-affecting change in the workspace; equal across installations built from the same state. Carried to audit so a decision can be tied to the policy state that produced it.

audience.description: Who may enforce this bundle. The runtime rejects a bundle whose audience does not equal its own whoami identity.

not_after.description: Hard expiry. At or after this instant the bundle decides nothing: every call is denied with policy_bundle_expired. At most 24 hours after issued_at.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Advised polling interval. The runtime clamps it to [30, 300] and applies +/-10% jitter.

stale_after_seconds.description: How long after the last successful refresh check the runtime reports the stale_but_valid state. Enforcement continues until not_after.

subject_resolution.description: How the PEP learns a human subject's user id, link state, effective groups and org roles. v1 supports two modes: online (deprecated, removed after transition) and bundle. In online mode the PEP calls POST /api/v1/runtime/subject-attributes:resolve. In bundle mode the PEP reads subject attributes from the bundle's identities array (ADR-034).

mode.description: online is withdrawn (ADR-026 G0) and retained only for backward compatibility during transition. bundle is the replacement (ADR-034).

max_cache_seconds.description: The longest a resolved subject may be reused in memory by a long-running PEP. Per-call subprocesses do not cache. In bundle mode this field is ignored (the bundle refresh cadence governs staleness).

agent_connector_bindings.description: Which connector capabilities each assigned agent is bound to. A connector call by an unbound agent is denied before policy is evaluated.

identities.description: Remote-identity table for subject resolution in bundle mode (ADR-034). Present when subject_resolution.mode is bundle. The PEP matches the incoming subject token's user_id or (source, external_id) against this array to resolve group memberships, org roles and link status. Required when subject_resolution.mode is bundle.

source.description: The exact system this remote identity is linked from (e.g. discord, slack, teams, github, entra, whatsapp, cli). Open set, not an enum.

external_id.description: The user's ID on that source.

user_id.description: The Kei user UUID this identity is linked to.

status.description: Link status. revoked takes effect at the next bundle refresh and ends the in-memory session. cross_workspace never falls through to a permit.

groups.description: Effective group memberships for this identity in this workspace.

org_roles.description: Effective org-level roles for this identity.

subject_token.description: An embedded subject token for offline-capable runtimes. When present the PEP may use this token instead of the session token for claim extraction. Optional.

expire_time.description: When this identity binding expires. After this instant the identity is treated as revoked.

harness_match_semantics.description: The dialect renderers (kei harness sync) apply when compiling policy into native harness permissions (ADR-029 section 1.4); no runtime component evaluates harness tool calls against it: argv-token prefix matching for shell:, exact skill:, path: globs, mcp:<server>[.<tool>], tool: names of registered harness tools, harness: sources, and the rule that a shell command is permitted only by a shell: permit with a literal token. policy_set.match_semantics (kei.match/v1) is unchanged. Present if and only if harnesses is present.

harnesses.description: The coding-agent harnesses registered on the audience installation (ADR-029 section 2; abac.runtime_installation_harnesses). Installation state, so it sits at the bundle root rather than in the workspace policy_set. Absent means no harness is registered and kei harness sync renders nothing. Adding, changing or deleting a harness re-issues the bundle with a new bundle_version.

harness.description: One registered harness. Identity is (installation_id, agent_id) — no surrogate id (3NF, amendment A2). Matched by harness:<agent_id> or harness:<kind>.

agent_id.description: The harness identity. Matched by harness:<agent_id> source. Never equal to a kind value.
